correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the signed-mode solution of the actual replicator law with fixed anchors as in equations (1)–(2). Put c=2p, A(v)=c(1−v)+v; the reduced dynamics preserve 0<u≤a and 0<v<1, and the sign of v′ is the sign of ρ−c². A(v)≥min(c,1) makes u track the limiting equilibrium a v∞/A(v∞) by variation of constants. A strictly interior limiting v away from the critical parameter would then have nonzero limiting derivative. At criticality v=η exactly. Subcritically u/v solves a forced linear equation with coefficient tending to c, so u/v→a/c and (v⁻²)′→2(c²−ρ)a²/c². Averaging proves both stated square-root limits. The argument covers p=1 and a=1 without any irreducibility assumption. The uploaded finite checks were inspected, not run; they are not the proof.
residual_risks: No transverse stability or attraction away from the exact opposed-opinion, equal-leadership family is established.

checked_sources: arXiv:2606.05825v1, equilibrium and individual leadership results
value.rationale: The equitable cross-mass ansatz is a natural network test case rather than an arbitrary numerical slice: it allows directed, unequally sized communities with arbitrary wiring at fixed exposure. The neutral critical family, endpoint selection, and exact nonexponential subcritical relaxation separate dynamical phenomena that equilibrium conditions alone cannot measure. The independence of the leading opinion amplitude from the initial polarization and leadership is a useful precise prediction on that family.
residual_risks: No claim of robustness under imperfect community balance, empirical predictive accuracy, or general network stability.
